speaker: Doctor
text: Patient, can you tell me when you first noticed the double vision and the weakness in your upper limbs? Has it been getting progressively worse?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any difficulty in climbing stairs recently, and does this difficulty occur every time you try to climb, or is it more intermittent? Additionally, do you feel more fatigued now compared to before these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you noticed any changes in your bowel or bladder function? Also, could you describe if there is any pain or discomfort associated with the weakness in your limbs? 

REQUEST TEST: Electromyography (EMG)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

Based on your symptoms of double vision that worsens with certain eye movements, upper limb and lower limb weakness that improves with rest, and the absence of numbness or balance problems, coupled with the information that the weakness is symmetrical and exacerbated by exertion, Myasthenia Gravis is a strong possibility. The requested EMG test will help confirm the diagnosis.
